content.text: All responsive locations checked: §9 termination rights, §29.4 notice period, §8 term/renewal, §10 wind-down, §7 fees. No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere, and no early-termination fee attaches to Customer's without-cause right.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets our preferred T4C position, so no redline is warranted. (1) Section 9.4 gives Customer an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause — a convenience right notwithstanding the absence of the word "convenience". (2) Section 29.4 fixes the Section 9.4 notice period at "thirty days before the effective termination date", within the 30-day preferred ceiling. (3) Section 9.4 caps Customer's exposure to accrued Fees only (no early-termination fee or penalty), and requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, reinforced by Section 10.2 ("refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination") — a pro-rata refund in substance. (4) Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year committed term: Section 9.1 (material breach) and 9.2 (insolvency) are for-cause only and mutual, Sections 9.3 and 9.4 run in Customer's favour alone, and Section 24.4 expressly denies Vendor a termination right on Customer change of control. Section 8.2's non-renewal mechanic is likewise exercisable only by Customer, and natural-term non-renewal falls under RENEWAL in any event. Note for the file: Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-mechanics term addressed under the liquidated-damages rule, not an early-termination fee, so it is not flagged here.
